descriptionAdvanced.en: Aqualeón is a unique leisure destination located in Albinyana, Catalonia, combining a full-scale water park with a wildlife safari experience. Situated in a beautiful natural setting between the sea and the mountains, the park offers a wide range of aquatic attractions, including high-speed slides, wave pools, and dedicated areas for younger children. The safari portion of the park allows visitors to observe large animals such as lions, tigers, and bears from the safety of specialized buses, providing an educational glimpse into the lives of these majestic creatures. Aqualeón emphasizes the importance of biodiversity and animal welfare, integrating entertainment with environmental awareness. It is a popular destination for families looking for a day of adventure and learning in the Mediterranean sunshine. The park's diverse offerings make it a standout attraction in the Costa Dorada region. Science K3 – Animal Habitats and Leisure Geography.

en: Aqualeón covers more than 800,000 square meters of natural space.
The park features over 12 major water slides, including the 'Kamikaze'.
Home to more than 300 animals from various global ecosystems.
Includes one of the largest wave pools in the Tarragona province.
The safari tour lasts approximately 30 minutes through different enclosures.
Participates in European programs for the conservation of endangered species.
The park is located just 15 kilometers from the Mediterranean coast.
Features a specialized flight show with birds of prey and parrots.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Barcelona Zoo, located within the historic Parc de la Ciutadella, is one of Spain's oldest and most respected zoological institutions. Since its opening in 1892, it has evolved into a center for conservation, research, and education, housing a vast collection of species from around the world. The zoo is famously known as the former home of Snowflake, the world's only known albino gorilla, who became a symbol of the city. Today, the zoo focuses on protecting endangered Mediterranean and global fauna, participating in numerous breeding programs. Its layout includes specialized habitats like the Land of Dragons, the Gorilla Space, and the Reptile House. The zoo's central urban location makes it an accessible and vital green space for both locals and tourists. It continues to modernize its facilities to prioritize animal welfare and provide immersive educational experiences for all ages. Science K3 – Urban Biodiversity and Conservation.

en: Barcelona Zoo covers approximately 13 hectares within the Ciutadella Park.
Home to over 2,000 animals representing more than 300 different species.
Famous for housing Snowflake (Floquet de Neu), the albino gorilla, for 37 years.
Participates in over 90 European Endangered Species Programs (EEP).
The Reptile House features one of the most significant collections in Europe.
The 'Land of Dragons' area is dedicated to Komodo dragons and island fauna.
Attracts more than 1 million visitors annually.
Features a historic 19th-century entrance and several modernist sculptures.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The San Sebastián Aquarium, located at the end of the picturesque harbor in the Basque Country, is one of Europe's most modern and interactive maritime museums. Housed in a historic building dating back to 1928, it underwent a major renovation to include a spectacular 360-degree acrylic tunnel that allows visitors to walk through a massive oceanarium filled with sharks and rays. The museum section offers a deep dive into the maritime history of the Basque people, showcasing their legendary relationship with the sea, from whaling traditions to modern shipbuilding. The aquarium emphasizes the conservation of the Bay of Biscay's biodiversity, featuring numerous tanks dedicated to local marine life. It serves as both a premier tourist attraction and a research center dedicated to oceanographic studies. The stunning views of the Concha Bay from its terraces add to the overall experience. Science K3 – Marine Ecosystems and Maritime History.

en: One of the oldest oceanographic museums in Spain, founded in 1928.
The main oceanarium contains over 1.5 million liters of seawater.
Features a 360-degree underwater tunnel, the first of its kind in Spain.
Home to more than 5,000 individual marine creatures from 40 species.
The skeleton of a North Atlantic right whale, caught in 1878, is a centerpiece.
Includes 31 specialized tanks representing different marine environments.
Attracts over 300,000 visitors per year to the Donostia waterfront.
The building was designed by renowned architect Juan Carlos Guerra.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The National Museum of Natural Sciences (MNCN) in Madrid is Spain's premier institution for the study and dissemination of natural history. Founded by King Charles III in 1771 as the Royal Cabinet of Natural History, it is one of the oldest museums of its kind in the world. Located in the beautiful Palacio de las Artes y la Industria, the museum houses millions of specimens covering zoology, geology, and paleontology. Its permanent exhibitions feature iconic displays such as the skeleton of a Megatherium sent from Argentina in 1789 and a magnificent Diplodocus replica. The museum is a major research center under the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC), contributing to global scientific knowledge on biodiversity and climate change. Its educational programs inspire thousands of students annually, fostering a deeper understanding of the natural world and the importance of environmental preservation. Science K3 – Paleontology and Earth Sciences.

en: Houses a collection of more than 6 million biological and geological specimens.
Founded in 1771, making it one of the oldest natural history museums globally.
The Megatherium skeleton was the first fossil skeleton ever mounted in the world.
Features a famous replica of a Diplodocus carnegii, gifted by Andrew Carnegie.
The museum is divided into three main sections: Biodiversity, Geology, and Evolution.
Employs over 70 permanent researchers and hundreds of visiting scientists.
The Mediterranean forest exhibit includes a detailed diorama of local ecosystems.
Located on the Paseo de la Castellana, part of Madrid's 'Golden Mile' of culture.

descriptionAdvanced.en: CosmoCaixa Barcelona is a world-class interactive science museum that offers an engaging exploration of the laws of nature and the universe. Its most iconic feature is the 'Flooded Forest' (Bosc Inundat), a 1,000-square-meter recreation of an Amazonian rainforest ecosystem, complete with tropical rain, caimans, and giant fish. Visitors can also explore the 'Geological Wall', which showcases different rock formations and tectonic processes, and the 'Universe Gallery', which traces the history of the cosmos from the Big Bang to the present. The museum is designed to be hands-on, encouraging visitors of all ages to experiment and discover scientific principles for themselves. CosmoCaixa is housed in a beautifully restored modernist building with a striking modern expansion, earning it the European Museum of the Year Award in 2006. It stands as a beacon of scientific literacy and curiosity in Catalonia. Science K3 – Environmental Science and Physics.

en: The 'Flooded Forest' contains over 100 species of Amazonian plants and animals.
Features a planetarium with advanced digital projection for astronomical shows.
The museum covers a total floor area of over 50,000 square meters.
The Geological Wall consists of 7 large sections of real rock totaling 90 tons.
Named European Museum of the Year in 2006 for its innovative displays.
Includes the 'Click and Flash' interactive area specifically for young children.
The building was originally built in 1904 as an asylum for the blind.
The outdoor 'Science Square' features large-scale acoustic and physical experiments.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The City of Arts and Sciences (Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias) is a breath-taking architectural and cultural complex in Valencia, designed by Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela. Located in the former bed of the Turia River, this futuristic 'city within a city' is one of the 12 Treasures of Spain. The complex includes several distinct structures: the Hemisfèric (an IMAX cinema and planetarium), the Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe (an interactive science museum), the Umbracle (a landscaped walk), the Oceanogràfic (Europe's largest aquarium), the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía (an opera house), and the Ágora. The science museum itself follows the philosophy of 'not touching is forbidden', making science accessible through hundreds of interactive exhibits. The complex's white, organic forms and surrounding turquoise pools have become a global symbol of modern Valencia and a top destination for architecture and science enthusiasts. Science K3 – Modern Engineering and Interactive Learning.

en: The complex spans a total length of nearly 2 kilometers along the Turia gardens.
The Museu de les Ciències is designed to resemble the skeleton of a whale.
The Hemisfèric resembles a giant human eye that can 'blink' over a pool.
The Oceanogràfic is the largest aquarium in Europe with 42 million liters of water.
Over 12,000 tons of steel were used in the construction of the Museu de les Ciències.
The complex has served as a filming location for movies like 'Tomorrowland' and 'Westworld'.
Attracts more than 4 million visitors per year from all over the world.
The Palau de les Arts is one of the world's tallest opera houses at 75 meters.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Terra Mítica is a major theme park in Benidorm, Costa Blanca, that takes visitors on a journey through the ancient civilizations of the Mediterranean. The park is divided into thematic zones representing Egypt, Greece, Rome, Iberia, and the Islands, each meticulously designed with authentic architecture and atmosphere. Thrilling attractions like the 'Magnus Colossus' wooden roller coaster and the 'Titanide' inverted coaster provide adrenaline for thrill-seekers, while numerous family rides and spectacular live shows recreate historical myths and legends. The park's location on a hillside offers stunning views of the Benidorm skyline and the sea. Terra Mítica combines historical education with modern entertainment, making it a unique destination that celebrates the cultural roots of the Mediterranean basin. It is a key player in the tourism economy of the Valencian Community. History K5 – Ancient Civilizations and Leisure Tourism.

en: The park is divided into 5 thematic areas based on Mediterranean history.
The 'Magnus Colossus' was once the longest wooden roller coaster in Europe.
Features the 'Synkope', a giant rotating pendulum that reaches 90 km/h.
The Egypt zone features a detailed recreation of the Port of Alexandria.
Includes an extensive area of water rides and pools for summer cooling.
The park covers over 1 million square meters of themed space.
Offers more than 20 daily shows including gladiatorial combat and myths.
Opened in the year 2000 as part of a major regional development project.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Isla Mágica is a popular theme park located in Seville, situated on the former grounds of the Expo '92 world's fair on the Isla de la Cartuja. The park is themed around the 16th-century Spanish Golden Age and the Age of Discovery, inviting visitors to explore various zones like the Gateway to the Indies, Amazonia, and the Pirates' Lair. Attractions range from the thrilling 'Jaguar' inverted roller coaster to the refreshing 'Anaconda' water ride. One of the park's highlights is the 'El Desafío' drop tower, themed as a Moorish minaret. Isla Mágica also features a large lake where spectacular night shows with pyrotechnics and water projections take place. The park successfully blends Seville's rich historical legacy with modern amusement, providing an educational and fun experience that highlights Spain's maritime past. It also includes 'Agua Mágica', a dedicated water park area. History K6 – Age of Discovery and Urban Development.

en: Built on the site of the 1992 Universal Exposition in Seville.
The 'Jaguar' was the first inverted roller coaster installed in Spain.
The park is divided into 7 thematic areas representing different historical eras.
Features 'Agua Mágica', known as the 'Beach of Seville' within the park.
The 'El Desafío' tower is 68 meters high and has 6 different drop modes.
The lake's night show uses one of the largest water screens in Europe.
The park's architecture faithfully recreates 16th-century colonial styles.
Provides an important green and leisure space for the city of Seville.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Parque Warner Madrid is one of the most important and visited theme parks in Europe, located in San Martín de la Vega near the Spanish capital. Dedicated to the world of Warner Bros. movies and characters, the park is divided into five themed areas: Hollywood Boulevard, Movie World Studios, DC Super Heroes World, Old West Territory, and Cartoon Village. It boasts some of the tallest and fastest roller coasters in Spain, such as 'Stunt Fall' and 'Superman: La Atracción de Acero'. Fans of all ages can meet their favorite characters, from Looney Tunes to Batman and the Justice League. The park offers world-class stunt shows and parades, creating a truly cinematic experience. In the summer, 'Parque Warner Beach' provides a refreshing water-themed expansion. It is a major economic driver for the Madrid region, attracting millions of film and thrill enthusiasts annually. Arts K8 – Cinema History and Mass Media.

en: Opened in 2002 as a joint venture between Warner Bros. and local investors.
The 'Superman' coaster features a 55-meter drop and reaches 100 km/h.
Stunt Fall is one of the few Giant Inverted Boomerang coasters in the world.
The park covers over 150 hectares, including the Warner Beach area.
Cartoon Village is the largest children's area in Spain.
Features the 'Venganza del Enigma', the tallest drop tower in Europe at 115m.
The Wild West area includes a 30,000 square meter wooden coaster, 'Coaster-Express'.
Hosts a spectacular night parade with Looney Tunes characters every day.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Puy du Fou España is a groundbreaking historical theme park located near Toledo, based on the award-winning French concept. Unlike traditional parks, Puy du Fou does not have roller coasters or mechanical rides; instead, it focuses on massive, live-action theatrical performances that bring Spanish history to life. Visitors can witness the exploits of El Cid, the voyage of Christopher Columbus, and the Golden Age of Spanish literature through spectacular shows with hundreds of actors, horses, and special effects. The park features meticulously recreated period villages where artisans demonstrate traditional crafts. Its nighttime show, 'El Sueño de Toledo', is the largest in Spain, involving a massive stage and over 200 performers. Puy du Fou offers a unique 'emotional journey' through the roots of Spanish culture, combining art, nature, and history in a way that captivates both children and adults. History K8 – National Heritage and Performing Arts.

en: The nighttime show 'El Sueño de Toledo' takes place on a 5-hectare stage.
Voted 'Best Park in the World' by multiple international tourism awards.
Features over 30 hectares of nature and historical village recreations.
The 'Allende la Mar Oceana' show is an immersive journey inside a 1492 ship.
Employs over 700 people including actors, riders, and master craftsmen.
The park's horses are trained in specialized equestrian centers on-site.
Located just 10 minutes from the historic UNESCO city of Toledo.
Includes 'El Arrabal', a traditional medieval market area with authentic food.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Bioparc Fuengirola is a small but highly influential zoological park on the Costa del Sol, famous for its 'zoo-immersion' design and focus on tropical forest ecosystems. It replaces the traditional cage system with hidden barriers, allowing visitors to feel as though they are walking through the jungles of Madagascar, Equatorial Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Indo-Pacific. The park is renowned for its breeding success with endangered species like the Sumatran tiger and the western lowland gorilla. A centerpiece of the park is a massive replica of a fallen baobab tree, which has become an icon of Fuengirola. The park's layout is designed to be explored in a circular route, offering intimate views of animals in habitats that prioritize their psychological and physical well-being. It is a pioneer in sustainable zoo management and environmental education in southern Spain. Science K3 – Tropical Biodiversity and Habitat Design.

en: Known as one of the best 'small-format' zoos in the world.
Home to the only breeding pair of Sumatran tigers in Spain.
The giant 'Baobab Tree' is 25 meters tall and serves as a primate habitat.
Participates in over 40 European Endangered Species breeding programs.
Features a specialized nocturnal area to observe animals active at night.
The park focuses heavily on forest conservation in Southeast Asia.
Located in the heart of Fuengirola, making it easily accessible by train.
Opened in 2001, completely transforming the town's old 1970s zoo.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Selwo Aventura is a large-scale safari and adventure park located in Estepona, Málaga, offering a unique blend of wildlife observation and outdoor activities. Spanning across a vast hilly territory, the park allows visitors to see animals from Africa and other continents in large, semi-free enclosures that mimic their natural habitats. The experience includes safari truck tours through the Great Lakes and the Valley of the Predators. Beyond wildlife, Selwo offers adventure activities such as the longest zip-line in Europe over a lake and several suspension bridges. The park is committed to conservation and education, hosting species like elephants, cheetahs, and giraffes. Visitors can also stay overnight in the 'Selwo Lodge', providing a more immersive African-style safari experience on the Andalusian coast. It is a premier destination for nature lovers and families seeking an active holiday. Science K3 – Wildlife Management and Savanna Ecosystems.

en: Covers an area of more than 100 hectares of rugged Mediterranean landscape.
Home to the only born-in-Spain African elephant in its first few years.
The 'Ziwa' zip-line is 116 meters long and crosses over a large lake.
Features 3 large suspension bridges reaching up to 65 meters in length.
The safari tour is conducted in off-road vehicles for a realistic feel.
Includes a bird canyon, one of the largest natural aviaries in Europe.
The Selwo Lodge offers cabins themed after African villages like Watu or Masai.
Actively participates in global projects for the protection of the Iberian lynx.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Cabárceno Natural Park, located in Cantabria, is a unique wildlife recovery center and zoo situated in a spectacular former open-pit iron mine. Unlike any other park in Europe, Cabárceno spans 750 hectares of karst landscape where animals live in massive enclosures, some exceeding tens of hectares. The animals find themselves in an environment very similar to their original habitats, allowing for natural behaviors and social structures. Visitors explore the park via a 20-kilometer road network by car or using a modern cable car system that offers a bird's-eye view of the brown bears, elephants, and rhinos. The park is globally recognized for its research and breeding success, particularly with African elephants. It is not just a tourist attraction but a vital center for environmental education and the preservation of endangered species in a stunning northern Spanish setting. Science K3 – Karst Geomorphology and Wildlife Recovery.

en: Located in a former iron mine that dates back to Roman times.
Spans 750 hectares, making it one of the largest wildlife parks in Europe.
Features over 20 kilometers of roads for visitors to drive through.
The cable car system has 4 lines and a total length of 6 kilometers.
Home to more than 1,000 animals from 100 species across five continents.
Boasts one of the most successful African elephant breeding groups in captivity.
The brown bear enclosure covers 35 hectares of natural terrain.
The park's unique karst landscape is characterized by red soil and limestone peaks.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Tibidabo Amusement Park is a historic landmark in Barcelona, perched on the highest peak of the Collserola Ridge. Opened in 1901, it is the oldest amusement park in Spain and the third oldest in Europe. The park offers a charming blend of vintage charm and modern thrills, with iconic attractions like the 'Avió' (a 1928 airplane simulator) and the 'Talaia' (a 1921 lookout tower). Modern additions like the 'Vértigo' roller coaster provide contemporary excitement. The park's most unique feature is its unparalleled panoramic view of Barcelona and the Mediterranean Sea. Adjacent to the park is the Sagrat Cor church, whose neo-Gothic spires dominate the skyline. Tibidabo remains a beloved part of Barcelona's identity, providing a magical atmosphere that bridges the gap between the city's past and present. It is easily accessible via a historic funicular railway. History K8 – Urban Leisure and Industrial Heritage.

en: Located 512 meters above sea level on Mount Tibidabo.
Founded in 1899 and opened its first attractions in 1901.
The 'Avió' was the world's first flight simulator, installed in 1928.
The Automaton Museum houses a world-renowned collection of 19th-century machines.
The 'Talaia' lookout arm lifts visitors to a height of 550m above sea level.
Featured in the movie 'Vicky Cristina Barcelona' by Woody Allen.
Accessible via the historic Blue Tram (Tramvia Blau) and a funicular.
The park covers 7 hectares and is divided into six thematic levels.

descriptionAdvanced.en: L'Aquàrium de Barcelona, located in the Port Vell area, is the world's most important center for Mediterranean marine life. It features 35 tanks that house over 11,000 animals from 450 different species. The highlight of the visit is the massive Oceanarium, which is traversed by an 80-meter long transparent tunnel, providing an immersive experience surrounded by sharks, rays, and moray eels. Specialized sections explore tropical seas and unique Mediterranean ecosystems. The aquarium is also home to 'Planeta Aqua', an educational area focusing on how life adapts to different aquatic environments, including a penguin colony and a tank with piranhas. As a leading marine research and conservation hub, it plays a vital role in educating the public about the importance of protecting the oceans. Its prime location in Barcelona's harbor makes it a top destination for international visitors. Science K3 – Mediterranean Marine Biology.

en: The Oceanarium is 36 meters in diameter and 5 meters deep.
The 80-meter underwater tunnel is one of the longest in the world.
Home to more than 11,000 marine creatures representing 450 species.
Features a dedicated area for the study of seahorses and their breeding.
Offers a unique 'Shark Diving' experience for qualified divers.
Attracts over 1.5 million visitors per year to the Port Vell district.
Includes the 'Explora!' interactive children's area with over 50 activities.
Participates in the 'SOS-Ocean' project for Mediterranean biodiversity.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Dinópolis is a major paleontological and scientific park located in Teruel, Aragon, dedicated to the world of dinosaurs. The park combines museum-quality exhibits with thematic attractions, based on the rich fossil discoveries made in the surrounding region. Visitors can explore the 'Palaeontology Museum', which houses one of the world's best collections of dinosaur fossils, including the remains of 'Turiasaurus riodevensis', one of the largest dinosaurs ever found in Europe. Interactive rides like 'Travel through Time' and 'The Last Minute' take guests through the history of the Earth and the evolution of species. Dinópolis is part of a larger network of smaller fossil sites across the province, making Teruel a global reference point for palaeontology. The park effectively bridges the gap between rigorous scientific research and popular entertainment, sparking curiosity about prehistoric life. Science K3 – Palaeontology and Evolution.

en: Teruel is home to the Turiasaurus riodevensis, one of Europe's largest dinosaurs.
The main museum features over 1,000 original fossils and life-size replicas.
Dinópolis consists of a main park and 7 smaller centers throughout the province.
Includes a 3D cinema and a 'T-Rex' animatronic show with cutting-edge technology.
More than 3 million people have visited the park since its opening in 2001.
The park's foundation conducts active excavations in the Teruel fossil basins.
The 'Sauriopark' area offers dinosaur-themed rides for younger children.
The museum is recognized as a 'site of cultural interest' by the Spanish government.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Katmandu Park, located in Magaluf, Mallorca, is an award-winning 'theme-aquarium' and interactive park known for its imaginative storytelling and high-tech attractions. The park's center-piece is 'The House', an upside-down Tibetan-themed mansion filled with optical illusions, interactive games, and robotic creatures. Other highlights include the '4D Experience', 'Desperados' interactive theater, and 'Katlantis' Splash Park for cooling off in the Balearic heat. The park's theme revolves around the legend of the Red Yeti and the mythical world of Katmandu. It has been consistently voted as one of the best theme parks in Spain by travel platforms. Katmandu Park offers a more intimate and surreal experience compared to larger traditional parks, focusing on sensory engagement and family fun. It is a key element of the modern leisure offering on the island of Mallorca. Arts K8 – Mythical Storytelling and Digital Leisure.

en: Voted 'Best Theme Park in Spain' by TripAdvisor multiple times.
The iconic 'Upside Down House' features 8 themed interactive rooms.
Includes a 36-hole 'Expedition Golf' course themed after legends.
Katlantis Splash Park features a multi-level fortress with over 150 water elements.
Features the 'K-3 Climb', a 16-meter high rope adventure course.
The 4D cinema uses moving seats and environmental effects like wind and smell.
Part of the Sol Katmandu Park & Resort, a pioneer in integrated family stays.
The park's mascot is Boro the Great, a friendly red Yeti.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Aqualandia, situated in Benidorm, is one of Spain's oldest and most iconic water parks, having opened its doors in 1985. It is set in a beautiful natural environment with lush vegetation and features a wide variety of slides and pools that use water drawn directly from local wells and then purified. The park is home to 'Verti-Go', one of the world's tallest capsule slides, offering a near-vertical drop for extreme thrill-seekers. For families, the park provides large wave pools, lagoons with waterfalls, and dedicated children's areas like 'Adventureland'. Aqualandia's extensive facilities, including picnic areas and restaurants, make it a full-day destination. Its enduring popularity has made it a cornerstone of Benidorm's leisure industry and a pioneer in the European water park sector. It is often visited in combination with the nearby Mundomar marine park. Physics K7 – Fluid Dynamics and Gravity.

en: Opened in 1985 as the first large-scale water park in Spain.
Verti-Go features two slides at heights of 28 and 33 meters.
The 33-meter Verti-Go slide is the highest capsule slide in Europe.
The park covers an area of 150,000 square meters on a hillside.
The Big-Bang attraction offers 4 different slides with varying intensity.
Includes the 'Atlantic Surf' wave pool, one of the largest in the region.
Utilizes a sophisticated water recycling and treatment system.
The 'Amazon' attraction is a slow river designed for relaxation and sightseeing.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Oasis Wildlife Fuerteventura is the largest zoological and botanical park in the Canary Islands, covering nearly 1 million square meters of volcanic terrain. The park is unique for its massive botanical garden featuring thousands of species of cacti and succulents from around the world. As a wildlife refuge, it is home to over 3,000 animals and is particularly famous for its camel recovery center and one of the largest camel herds in Europe. Visitors can experience camel safaris along the coast or through the park's interior. Oasis Wildlife is deeply committed to the conservation of native Canarian species and global endangered wildlife, including the Cuvier's gazelle. The park's educational shows emphasize the fragility of desert ecosystems and the importance of sustainable agriculture. It is an essential stop for nature enthusiasts visiting the island of Fuerteventura. Science K3 – Island Biogeography and Desert Flora.

en: The largest theme park in the Canary Islands, spanning 1 million square meters.
Home to more than 3,000 animals from over 250 different species.
Features the largest botanical garden of cacti and succulents in Europe.
The camel herd consists of over 400 individuals, used for research and safaris.
Includes a specialized farm for the recovery of the Majorero donkey breed.
Participates in 45 European Endangered Species Programs (EEP).
The park produces its own organic animal feed on-site.
Offers four educational live shows: Sea Lions, Birds of Prey, Parrots, and Reptiles.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Rancho Texas Lanzarote Park is a popular western-themed animal and water park located in Puerto del Carmen. It offers a unique combination of wildlife exhibits, spectacular shows, and aquatic fun. The park's theme pays homage to the historical links between the Canary Islands and the founding of San Antonio, Texas. Visitors can see a variety of animals, including white tigers, Komodo dragons, and American bison. The park is famous for its sea lion and dolphin shows, as well as its impressive bird of prey demonstrations. For relaxation, the 'Corral' area features swimming pools and water slides. Rancho Texas provides an engaging educational experience focusing on animal training and conservation, all within a beautifully landscaped environment that mimics the American West and the local volcanic terrain. It is a top-rated attraction for families on the island of Lanzarote. Science K3 – Animal Training and Cultural Geography.

en: The park's name refers to the 18 Canary Island families who founded San Antonio.
Home to one of the few pairs of white tigers in Spain.
Features a modern dolphinarium with three pools containing 5 million liters of water.
The 'Eagle Show' features birds of prey flying freely over the audience.
Includes a gold mine and a western town recreation for children.
The park uses volcanic stone and native plants in its landscape design.
Participates in international breeding programs for the Komodo dragon.
The water park area includes a splash zone and two large swimming pools.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Parque de Atracciones de Madrid is the city's traditional urban amusement park, located in the vast Casa de Campo parkland. Since its opening in 1969, it has been a favorite leisure spot for Madrilenians and visitors alike. The park is divided into several themed zones: Maquinismo (with high-adrenaline rides), Naturaleza, Tranquilidad, and Nickelodeon Land for younger kids. Thrilling highlights include the 'Abismo' roller coaster and the 'La Lanzadera' 63-meter drop tower. Unlike the movie-themed Warner Park, this park focuses on a wide variety of rides set within a lush, forested environment. It is easily accessible by the city's metro system, making it a convenient and green escape for families. The park frequently hosts concerts and events, maintaining its status as a core part of Madrid's social and recreational life for over five decades. History K8 – Urban Development and Mass Leisure.

en: Inaugurated in 1969 by Carlos Arias Navarro, then mayor of Madrid.
Abismo is a world-class coaster reaching 100 km/h with a 49-meter drop.
The 'Star Flyer' chair-o-plane ride stands 80 meters high with amazing city views.
Nickelodeon Land is the largest area in Spain dedicated to characters like SpongeBob.
The 'Tarántula' is a spinning roller coaster with 630 meters of track.
The park is directly connected to the Madrid Metro (Batán station).
Features a historic boat ride through a series of dioramas and caves.
Surrounded by the 1,700 hectares of the Casa de Campo public park.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Mundomar is a premier animal park in Benidorm, dedicated to marine mammals and exotic birds, emphasizing a close-contact and educational experience. Set against the backdrop of the Sierra Helada mountains, the park's lush tropical environment houses dolphins, sea lions, penguins, and lemurs, as well as a variety of parrots and flamingos. Mundomar is particularly famous for its high-quality dolphin and sea lion shows, which focus on the animals' natural abilities and the bond with their trainers. It offers unique 'encounter' programs where visitors can interact directly with dolphins or sea lions under expert supervision. The park is committed to conservation and provides therapeutic activities with dolphins for children with special needs. Its proximity to the Aqualandia water park makes it a key part of the leisure offering on the Costa Blanca. Science K3 – Marine Mammal Ethology and Conservation.

en: The dolphinarium is one of the most modern in Spain, holding 6 million liters of water.
Features a large colony of Humboldt penguins in a specialized rocky habitat.
The park offers 'dolphin-assisted therapy' programs for neurological disorders.
Visitors can walk through a giant aviary with over 20 species of exotic birds.
The sea lion show incorporates educational elements about ocean pollution.
Participates in European programs for the conservation of the squirrel monkey.
Offers panoramic views of Benidorm from its elevated viewpoint locations.
Intimately connected with Aqualandia, sharing some management and facilities.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Marineland Mallorca is a pioneer in marine mammal parks in Spain, located in Costa d'en Blanes near Palma. It was the first park in the country to feature dolphin and sea lion shows and has won numerous international awards for its quality and conservation efforts. The park's highlight is the dolphinarium, where the Atlantic bottlenose dolphins demonstrate their intelligence and agility. In addition to marine mammals, Marineland features an aquarium with Mediterranean and tropical species, a reptile house with crocodiles and snakes, and an aviary with colorful tropical birds. The park is dedicated to environmental education, offering workshops for schools to learn about marine ecosystems and the importance of biodiversity. Its location next to the beach and its manageable size make it an ideal half-day destination for families seeking an educational and entertaining experience in Mallorca. Science K3 – Marine Biodiversity and Public Education.

en: First dolphinarium in Spain, opening its doors in 1970.
Seven-time winner of the 'Best Dolphinarium in the World' award by IMATA.
Home to a group of Atlantic bottlenose dolphins known for their longevity.
The aquarium includes a dedicated area for sharks and rays.
The reptile house features a large collection of iguanas and caimans.
The bird show features free-flying macaws and cockatoos.
Participates in the 'European Association for Aquatic Mammals' (EAAM).
Located in a prime spot on the Calvià coast, just 10 minutes from Palma.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Guadalquivir River is the lifeblood of southern Spain, stretching 657 kilometers from its source in the Sierra de Cazorla to its mouth in the Atlantic Ocean at Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Its name, derived from the Arabic 'al-wadi al-kabir' (the great river), reflects its historical importance as a vital trade route since antiquity. During the Age of Discovery, it was the only navigable river in Spain, allowing treasure-laden galleons to sail directly into the heart of Seville. Today, it remains navigable up to Seville, making it the only inland commercial port in Spain. The river's lower course flows through the Doñana National Park, one of Europe's most significant wetlands. A xeno-historian would view this river as a legendary interplanetary trade route, linking the heart of an ancient terrestrial empire to the cosmic horizons. Geography K6 – River Systems and Maritime Trade.

en: The fifth-longest river in the Iberian Peninsula at 657 kilometers.
The only great navigable river in Spain for large vessels up to Seville.
The river basin covers 57,011 square kilometers, nearly 18% of Spain.
Played a central role in the trade monopoly with the Americas in the 16th century.
The Roman bridge in Córdoba has spanned its waters for over 2,000 years.
Forms a massive delta in the Doñana National Park, home to rare bird species.
The name Guadalquivir comes from the Arabic 'Wadi al-Kabir', meaning 'The Great Valley'.
Host to the first circumnavigation of the globe, as Magellan set sail from its shores.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Somiedo Natural Park, located in the heart of the Cantabrian Mountains in Asturias, is a wild sanctuary of rare beauty and a designated UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. This rugged landscape is defined by deep glacial valleys, shimmering alpine lakes, and imposing limestone peaks, offering one of the best-preserved ecosystems on the Iberian Peninsula. Somiedo is most famous for hosting the largest population of Cantabrian brown bears in Spain, making it a privileged location for observing these apex predators in their natural habitat. A unique cultural feature is the presence of 'teitos', traditional stone huts with thatched roofs used for centuries by transhumant shepherds. A xeno-biologist would designate this area 'Zone X-1' for the preservation of a flagship species and its ancient symbiotic relationship with human land-use traditions. Biology K8 – Ecosystem Conservation and Sustainable Architecture.

en: Declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2000 for its pristine environment.
Home to more than 40% of the Cantabrian brown bear population.
Features the 'Lagos de Saliencia', a group of four spectacular glacial lakes.
The park covers an area of approximately 291 square kilometers.
Includes over 500 'teitos', traditional huts with roofs made of broom grass.
Altitudes within the park range from 400 to 2,194 meters at Cornón Peak.
A haven for other rare species like the western capercaillie and the Iberian wolf.
One of the few places in Spain where traditional 'brañas' (pasture systems) are still active.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Bardenas Reales is a fascinating semi-desert territory in Navarre, offering a nearly extraterrestrial landscape that stands in stark contrast to the green areas of northern Spain. This 42,000-hectare UNESCO Biosphere Reserve is characterized by bizarre geological formations, deep canyons, and high plateaus called 'cabezos'. Erosion caused by wind and water on clay and sandstone soils has created spectacular natural sculptures, the most famous being 'Castildetierra', a solitary earthen tower that has become the park's symbol. An exo-geologist would study these stratified sedimentary rocks to reconstruct the region's complex climatic history. Due to its dramatic appearance, the area has served as a filming location for numerous international productions, including 'Game of Thrones'. It is an ideal destination for photographers and hikers seeking an otherworldly experience. Geology K9 – Erosion and Sedimentary Landscapes.

en: Declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2000.
Spans over 42,000 hectares in the southeastern part of Navarre.
Divided into three main areas: El Plano, Bardena Blanca, and Bardena Negra.
The highest point is the Cabezo de Aguilar at 600 meters.
A portion of the park is used as a military training range by the Spanish Air Force.
Temperatures vary extremely, from freezing in winter to over 40°C in summer.
The unique red and yellow colors come from iron and sulfur in the clay.
Home to various raptors, including Egyptian vultures and golden eagles.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Roman Bridge of Córdoba is an imposing historical monument spanning the Guadalquivir River, serving as the city's main entrance for nearly two thousand years. Built in the 1st century BC during the reign of Emperor Augustus, it was a vital part of the Via Augusta, the road connecting Rome to Cádiz. Although the visible structure has undergone numerous reconstructions during the Moorish and Christian periods, its foundations remain authentically Roman. An astro-engineer would view the longevity of these foundations as proof of superior construction techniques and materials, suitable for building planetary outposts. Its 16 arches reflect beautifully in the river, providing one of Córdoba's most iconic images, especially at sunset. Now pedestrian-only, it offers a peaceful walk with views of the Great Mosque-Cathedral, symbolizing the city's multilayered history. History K5 – Roman Infrastructure and Urban Continuity.

en: The bridge has 16 arches and is approximately 247 meters long.
Originally built in the 1st century BC as part of the primary road to Rome.
Was the only bridge in Córdoba across the Guadalquivir for 20 centuries.
Appeared in Season 5 of 'Game of Thrones' as the Long Bridge of Volantis.
The statue of Saint Raphael, the city's protector, was added in 1651.
The Calahorra Tower at the southern end now houses a museum of cultures.
The bridge's foundations have survived countless major river floods.
Forms part of the UNESCO World Heritage site of the Historic Center of Córdoba.

descriptionAdvanced.en: The Tower of Hercules in A Coruña, Galicia, is the oldest lighthouse in the world that remains in continuous operation today. Built by the Romans in the 2nd century AD, likely during the reign of Emperor Trajan, it has guided sailors through the treacherous waters of the Atlantic for nearly two millennia. An interstellar navigator would recognize it as a primitive but remarkably resilient navigational beacon, a terrestrial precursor to planetary beacon systems. While the current exterior is a neoclassical facade from the late 18th century, the authentic Roman core remains preserved within. Legend says the Greek hero Hercules buried the head of the giant Geryon here after defeating him, building the tower over the grave. Its UNESCO World Heritage status underlines its exceptional universal value as a symbol of maritime continuity. History K5 – Roman Maritime Technology.

en: The only Roman lighthouse in the world still in use.
Stands 55 meters tall, with its light visible from 23 nautical miles away.
Declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2009.
The original Roman core is visible inside the current 18th-century structure.
Features 234 steps leading up to the observation deck.
The architect of the 1788 restoration was Eustaquio Giannini.
Located on a 57-meter high cliff overlooking the Atlantic Ocean.
Surrounded by a sculpture park with 15 large-scale artworks.

descriptionAdvanced.en: Poblet Monastery is one of the largest and most complete Cistercian abbeys in the world, located in the province of Tarragona, Catalonia. Founded in the 12th century, this fortified monastery served as the royal pantheon for the Kings of Aragon, housing masterfully carved tombs that represent the pinnacle of Gothic funerary art. A cybernetic monk would analyze the structure as a highly efficient, self-sufficient system integrating spiritual contemplation, agriculture, and defense into a single unit. The complex is a masterpiece of Cistercian architecture, characterized by its austere beauty and harmonious proportions. Surrounded by massive walls and defense towers, it protected a vibrant community of monks and a vast library. Today, it remains an active monastery, where a community of Cistercians maintains centuries-old traditions of 'ora et labora'. History K6 – Medieval Monastic Life and Royal Patronage.

en: The largest Cistercian abbey still inhabited in the world.
Declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1991.
Contains the royal tombs of eight Kings and six Queens of Aragon.
The main cloister dates from the 12th to 14th centuries.
The monastery is protected by a fortified wall with 12 defense towers.
The library contains thousands of valuable volumes and historical documents.
The monks continue to produce their own wine in the surrounding vineyards.
Was abandoned in 1835 and underwent a major restoration starting in 1940.
